claim.summary: src/click/parser.py is Click's private argv parser, adapted from optparse. Core.Command.make_parser (core.py:1227) builds an _OptionParser(ctx), and each Parameter's add_to_parser registers itself. Command.parse_args (core.py:1371-1372) then calls parser.parse_args. The parser does no type conversion or defaults. It returns raw values in a dict keyed by dest, the leftover args, and a list of parameter objects in command-line order. Unset values are the UNSET sentinel, and FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE marks an option whose value was omitted. The old public names (OptionParser, Argument, Option, split_opt, normalize_opt, ParsingState, split_arg_string) are served by a module `__getattr__` that emits DeprecationWarning.

interfaces.name: _OptionParser
interfaces.behavior: Internal parser class. __init__(ctx=None) stores ctx and defaults allow_interspersed_args=True and ignore_unknown_options=False. If ctx is given, both flags are copied from ctx. It starts with _opt_prefixes={'-','--'}, plus empty _short_opt, _long_opt and _args. The docstring carries a '.. deprecated:: 8.2' note.
edge_cases: ctx=None disables token normalization and resilient parsing
Flags are copied once at construction, so later changes to ctx are not seen

interfaces.name: _OptionParser.add_option
interfaces.behavior: Normalizes each opt string with _normalize_opt (which applies ctx.token_normalize_func). It builds an _Option, adds its prefixes to _opt_prefixes, and registers its short opts in _short_opt and its long opts in _long_opt. The dest is passed in explicitly and never inferred. action defaults to 'store' and nargs to 1. Valid actions are store, store_const, append, append_const and count.
edge_cases: An opt with no prefix (starts alnum) raises ValueError from _Option
An unknown action is not checked here; it fails later in _Option.process
Re-registering an opt string silently overwrites the earlier one

interfaces.name: _OptionParser.add_argument
interfaces.behavior: Appends an _Argument(obj, dest, nargs) to _args. Positional order is the order of calls.
edge_cases: Two arguments with nargs<0 cause a TypeError later, in _unpack_args

interfaces.name: _OptionParser.parse_args
interfaces.behavior: Builds a _ParsingState(args), runs _process_args_for_options and then _process_args_for_args. It returns (state.opts, state.largs, state.order). The input list is consumed (popped) in place.
edge_cases: UsageError is swallowed when ctx.resilient_parsing is true, and the partial results are returned
With ctx=None the error always propagates

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._process_args_for_options
interfaces.behavior: Pops from rargs one arg at a time. A bare '--' stops processing and is dropped. An arg whose first character is in _opt_prefixes and whose length is >1 goes to _process_opts. Any other arg is appended to largs if interspersed args are allowed. Otherwise it is pushed back onto rargs and parsing stops.
edge_cases: A lone '-' is treated as positional
The '--' check uses `return`, so the remaining args stay in rargs

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._process_args_for_args
interfaces.behavior: Calls _unpack_args(largs+rargs, [nargs of each arg]) and then each _Argument.process. The leftovers become largs and rargs is cleared.
edge_cases: Extra positionals are returned as leftover args
Missing positionals are UNSET

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._process_opts
interfaces.behavior: Splits the arg on the first '=' to get an explicit value and normalizes the name. It tries _match_long_opt first, so single-dash long options like -foo match. On NoSuchOption it falls back to _match_short_opt if the arg's first two characters are not a registered prefix. For a '--x' arg it re-raises, unless ignore_unknown_options is set, in which case it appends the arg to largs.
edge_cases: An explicit '=value' on a short option is treated as part of the arg string

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._match_long_opt
interfaces.behavior: Looks the name up in _long_opt. A value-taking option has the explicit value inserted at rargs[0] and then reads its value through _get_value_from_state. A flag with an explicit value raises BadOptionUsage; otherwise its value is UNSET. It finishes with option.process.
edge_cases: Unknown opt raises NoSuchOption with possibilities=_long_opt for suggestions

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._match_short_opt
interfaces.behavior: Walks the characters of a clustered arg such as -abc. A value-taking option consumes the rest of the arg as its value. With ignore_unknown_options, unknown characters are collected and re-appended to largs as prefix+chars.
edge_cases: Each char is normalized individually
The prefix is arg[0]

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._get_value_from_state
interfaces.behavior: Takes nargs values from rargs. If fewer than nargs remain, it returns FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE when obj._flag_needs_value is set, and otherwise raises BadOptionUsage. For nargs==1, if the option allows an omitted value and the next arg looks like an option, it returns FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE instead of consuming it. For nargs>1 it returns a tuple.
edge_cases: The message is pluralized with ngettext

interfaces.name: _Option
interfaces.behavior: Holds obj, dest, action, nargs, const, prefixes, _short_opts and _long_opts. An opt is short if it has a 1-character prefix and a 1-character name; everything else is long. takes_value is true for the store and append actions. process(value, state) applies the action to state.opts and appends obj to state.order.
edge_cases: An opt with no prefix raises ValueError 'Invalid start character for option (x)'
An unknown action raises ValueError("unknown action '...'") at process time
count adds 1 starting from 0
append and append_const use setdefault(dest, [])

interfaces.name: _Argument
interfaces.behavior: Holds dest, nargs and obj. process(value, state) sets state.opts[dest]=value and appends obj to state.order. For nargs>1, a partial tuple (some UNSET) raises BadArgumentUsage, and an all-UNSET tuple becomes UNSET. An empty tuple (from nargs=-1 with nothing left) becomes UNSET.
edge_cases: Partial nargs>1 values raise
Empty variadic values are UNSET, not ()

interfaces.name: _ParsingState
interfaces.behavior: Mutable state with opts (dict), largs (list), rargs (the input list) and order (list of params).

interfaces.name: _unpack_args
interfaces.behavior: Distributes args across nargs_spec. A positive nargs takes that many, with UNSET fill for missing items (a tuple when nargs>1). A negative nargs takes all the remainder, and specs after it are filled from the right. It returns (tuple of values, leftover list).
edge_cases: Missing items are UNSET
The wildcard slot is a tuple, possibly empty

interfaces.name: _split_opt
interfaces.behavior: Returns (prefix, rest). An alnum first character gives ('', opt). A doubled first character gives (opt[:2], opt[2:]). Otherwise it returns (first, opt[1:]).
edge_cases: An empty string yields first='' and ('', '')

interfaces.name: _normalize_opt
interfaces.behavior: Applies ctx.token_normalize_func to the name part and keeps the prefix. It returns opt unchanged if ctx is None or no func is set.
edge_cases: ctx=None returns opt unchanged

interfaces.name: __getattr__
interfaces.behavior: Module-level shim. For OptionParser, Argument, Option, split_opt, normalize_opt and ParsingState, it emits a DeprecationWarning (stacklevel=2) and returns globals()['_'+name]. split_arg_string is lazily imported from click.shell_completion with its own warning.
edge_cases: Unknown names raise AttributeError(name)

claim.error_conventions: Usage problems raise click.exceptions subclasses. NoSuchOption is raised for unknown options and is given possibilities for suggestions. BadOptionUsage(option_name, msg) covers a missing value or a value attached to a flag. BadArgumentUsage covers a partial nargs on an argument. Messages are gettext-wrapped and formatted with {name!r}, for example "Option '--x' requires an argument." and "Option {name!r} requires {nargs} arguments." (pluralized with ngettext). Programmer errors use ValueError (invalid option prefix, unknown action) and TypeError (two variadic arguments). The module `__getattr__` raises AttributeError for unknown names and warns with DeprecationWarning.

examples.description: Default prefixes of a fresh parser
Custom prefixes are collected through Option.add_to_parser
examples.code:
ctx = click.Context(click.Command("test"))
parser = _OptionParser(ctx)
click.Option("+p", is_flag=True).add_to_parser(parser, ctx)
click.Option("!e", is_flag=True).add_to_parser(parser, ctx)
assert parser._opt_prefixes == {"-", "--", "+", "!"}

examples.description: Deprecated attribute access must be wrapped in pytest.warns
examples.code:
with pytest.warns(DeprecationWarning, match=name):
    value = getattr(module, name)
assert value == target

tests.how_it_asserts: Plain functions with bare asserts. They check the _opt_prefixes set on _OptionParser directly, with and without custom-prefix options added via Option.add_to_parser. Parsing behavior itself is mostly covered indirectly by tests/test_options.py and tests/test_arguments.py (not read here).

test_attr_deprecated is parametrized over (module, name, target). It uses pytest.warns(DeprecationWarning, match=name) around getattr and asserts equality with the _-prefixed target. test_unknown_attribute_raises expects AttributeError for click, click.core, click.parser and click.utils.

extension_points.name: Parameter.add_to_parser
extension_points.what_could_attach: The abstract hook (core.py:2516) that each Parameter subclass implements to register itself with the parser. Option's version is at core.py:3325 and Argument's at core.py:3800. A custom Parameter can call parser.add_option or add_argument with its own action and const.

extension_points.name: Command.make_parser
extension_points.what_could_attach: Subclasses can override it to return a customized _OptionParser subclass or to add extra options.

extension_points.name: _Option.process
extension_points.what_could_attach: The action dispatch if/elif chain. A new action such as 'extend' or 'store_true_once' would be added here, with takes_value updated to match.

extension_points.name: _OptionParser._opt_prefixes
extension_points.what_could_attach: The set of recognized option prefixes. It is extended automatically when options with new prefixes are added.

extension_points.name: _normalize_opt
extension_points.what_could_attach: Hooks into Context.token_normalize_func, for example for case-insensitive or alias normalization of option names.

gaps.description: Unknown-action validation at add_option time, so a bad action fails when registered rather than at parse time
gaps.why_plausible: _Option.__init__ already validates prefixes eagerly, but the action is only checked in process() (parser.py:181).

gaps.description: Detection of duplicate or conflicting option registrations
gaps.why_plausible: add_option silently overwrites entries in _short_opt and _long_opt (parser.py:285-288).

gaps.description: Unique-prefix abbreviation matching of long options (as argparse does)
gaps.why_plausible: _match_long_opt requires an exact match and only offers 'possibilities' for suggestions (parser.py:366-367).

gaps.description: Explicit '=value' support for short options, such as -o=value
gaps.why_plausible: The '=' split in _process_opts feeds only the long-option path. Short options fall back to _match_short_opt with the '=' as part of the value.

gaps.description: Direct unit tests of parse_args, _unpack_args and the error paths
gaps.why_plausible: tests/test_parser.py covers only the prefix sets, so direct parser-level tests are thin.

limitations: The module is private and deprecated; the docstring says it will be removed in Click 9.0, and the shim message points users to the stdlib optparse.
There is no type conversion or defaulting; everything is raw strings, UNSET or FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE.
Flags are copied from ctx once, in __init__.
Actions are plain strings dispatched through an if/elif chain.
No abbreviation matching of long options.
In resilient_parsing mode, UsageError is swallowed and partial results are returned.
I did not read tests/test_options.py, tests/test_arguments.py or tests/test_basic.py, which exercise the parser indirectly.
